---
title: "Oncoprints (mutation landscapes) in JavaScript with CanvasXpress"
description: "Draw a publication-style oncoprint — genes by tumours, with CNA and mutation overlays and per-gene frequencies — in the browser, from one portable spec."
author: "Isaac Neuhaus"
date: "2026-10-28"
categories: [JavaScript, CanvasXpress, oncoprint, bioinformatics, visualization]
image: "thumbnail.png"
---

An oncoprint is the standard way to show a **mutation landscape**: genes down one axis, tumours along
the other, each cell stacking the alterations that gene carries in that sample — copy-number
amplification/deletion plus mutation type. Building one in the browser from scratch is a lot of SVG
and sorting logic. CanvasXpress is a JavaScript library at heart, so it's a `Heatmap` with overlay
matrices.

## Load the library

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
```

## The markup and the spec

The base matrix is `data`; same-shaped `data2` (copy number) and `data3` (mutation) are the overlays,
each cell a string like `"Amplification"`, `"Missense"`, or `""`.

```html
<canvas id="onco" width="820" height="440"></canvas>
<script>
  var genes = ["TP53","KRAS","PIK3CA","PTEN","EGFR","BRAF","APC","RB1","NF1","MYC","CDKN2A","ARID1A"],
      samples = [], CNA = ["Amplification","Deletion"], MUT = ["Missense","Nonsense","Truncating"];
  for (var i = 0; i < 28; i++) samples.push("T" + (i + 1 < 10 ? "0" : "") + (i + 1));
  function pick(a) { return a[Math.floor(Math.random() * a.length)]; }

  var base = [], cna = [], mut = [];
  genes.forEach(function (g, gi) {
    var rate = Math.max(0.05, 0.5 * (1 - gi / genes.length)), b = [], c = [], m = [];
    samples.forEach(function () {
      b.push(Math.round((Math.random() * 4 - 2) * 100) / 100);
      c.push(Math.random() < rate * 0.5 ? pick(CNA) : "");
      m.push(Math.random() < rate ? pick(MUT) : "");
    });
    base.push(b); cna.push(c); mut.push(m);
  });

  var data = { y: { vars: genes, smps: samples, data: base, data2: cna, data3: mut } };
  var config = { graphType: "Heatmap", oncoprintCNA: "data2", oncoprintMUT: "data3",
                 overlaysThickness: 100, xAxis: samples,
                 title: "Mutation landscape: 12 genes across 28 tumours" };

  new CanvasXpress("onco", data, config);
</script>
```

## Live result

```{=html}
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
<canvas id="oncoLive" width="820" height="440"></canvas>
<script>
(function () {
  function draw() {
    if (typeof CanvasXpress === "undefined") { return setTimeout(draw, 60); }
    var genes = ["TP53","KRAS","PIK3CA","PTEN","EGFR","BRAF","APC","RB1","NF1","MYC","CDKN2A","ARID1A"],
        samples = [], CNA = ["Amplification","Deletion"], MUT = ["Missense","Nonsense","Truncating"];
    for (var i = 0; i < 28; i++) samples.push("T" + (i + 1 < 10 ? "0" : "") + (i + 1));
    function pick(a) { return a[Math.floor(Math.random() * a.length)]; }
    var base = [], cna = [], mut = [];
    genes.forEach(function (g, gi) {
      var rate = Math.max(0.05, 0.5 * (1 - gi / genes.length)), b = [], c = [], m = [];
      samples.forEach(function () {
        b.push(Math.round((Math.random() * 4 - 2) * 100) / 100);
        c.push(Math.random() < rate * 0.5 ? pick(CNA) : "");
        m.push(Math.random() < rate ? pick(MUT) : "");
      });
      base.push(b); cna.push(c); mut.push(m);
    });
    new CanvasXpress("oncoLive",
      { y: { vars: genes, smps: samples, data: base, data2: cna, data3: mut } },
      { graphType: "Heatmap", oncoprintCNA: "data2", oncoprintMUT: "data3", overlaysThickness: 100,
        xAxis: samples, title: "Mutation landscape: 12 genes across 28 tumours" });
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

canvasXpress sorts the waterfall for you and shows the alteration frequency per row. Hover a cell to
read the exact alteration; swap the overlays for your own MAF / CNA calls.

## Why "reproducible"

The base matrix, the overlays and the `config` **are** the figure — one portable JSON spec that
renders the same from R, Python, or a web page.
